name: Pop-Up Installations
description:
A pop-up installation temporarily places a designed intervention in a real or realistic environment so that people can encounter, use or respond to it. Unlike a laboratory prototype, the intervention becomes part of the surrounding context for a limited period.

This can help designers investigate how a proposition interacts with place, existing activities and people who may not have been recruited specifically for a conventional study.
whenToUse: Use a pop-up installation when spatial context, public interaction or situated experience is central to the concept and a temporary deployment is feasible.
steps: Define the question the installation should investigate.
Determine permissions, safety and accessibility requirements.
Create the minimum intervention needed to produce the intended encounter.
Install it for an appropriate period.
Observe how people encounter and interpret it.
Invite feedback where appropriate and ethical.
Document unexpected uses and contextual effects.
Remove the installation and analyse the findings.
lookOutFor: Public deployment introduces safety, consent, privacy and accessibility responsibilities.
People encountering the installation may not know they are part of a research activity.
Novelty effects can strongly influence behaviour during short deployments.

resources.citation: Tomitsch, M. et al. (2021). *Design. Think. Make. Break. Repeat*. BIS Publishers.
